title: Fix installation smoke lifecycle after active Outcome
outOfScope: Changing the installed Runtime coverage policy to advisory.
Changing production installer payload or release behavior.
Merging or relying on the superseded RFE-101/RFE-102 branch evidence.

sources.reason: Defines the governed branch, PR, closure, and explicit archive lifecycle.
Hosted installation-smoke failure log: strict coverage guard rejects installed Runtime files before their install commit.
Unmerged historical reference only; its workflow diff identifies the prior corrective ordering without serving as delivery evidence.

riskAssessment.reason: The fixture validates an adopter lifecycle and must not bypass strict coverage or human-report boundaries.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized continued planned remediation and explicit repair of discovered workflow defects.

preReviewWarnings: The workflow fixture may validate order mechanically, but must not claim a human saw a CI log; the real agent must relay the active Outcome before archive.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: installation-smoke conditionally runs explicit archive when ai-finish retains an active Contract, then proves an archive exists before git add/commit and post-install governance guards.
A static regression test rejects any workflow that moves archive after install commit or coverage guard.
The correction leaves strict coverage enforcement enabled and does not copy template tests into adopter payload merely to silence the guard.
Focused and full local verification pass; hosted installation-smoke passes on the corrective PR.
guidelines: Keep installed-adopter lifecycle evidence truthful: the fixture asserts command order, not human conversation delivery.
Fix the lifecycle boundary rather than weakening coverage enforcement or inflating the installer payload.

intent.problem: RFE-104 hosted CI installation-smoke failed because the temporary adopter invoked ai-finish, which now retains an active Outcome, then ran strict coverage guard against the pre-install baseline before its install commit. The guard correctly treated installed Runtime files as untested production changes.
constraints: Keep the active Outcome report-before-archive behavior.
Archive explicitly before the installer fixture commits the Runtime.
Do not modify immutable predecessor evidence or merge the superseded historical branch.
intent.rationale: An installer smoke test must model the same explicit archival transition required in real governed work; committing first erases the intended lifecycle boundary and makes first-install checks structurally impossible.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: User granted continuing authority for planned corrective Work Items, PRs, merges, and lifecycle closure.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff; this restores the previous fixture failure rather than weakening installed Runtime policy.
rawUserRequest: Continue the authorized plan. Repair discovered process problems before release; every Work Item must report directly while active before archive, then complete PR, CI, merge, and cleanup.

declaredIntent.summary: Repair the installed-adopter smoke fixture so it explicitly archives the active Outcome before committing the installed Runtime and evaluating post-install guards.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Fresh temporary adopter completes ai-finish, explicit archive, install commit, then status/backtrack/coverage/ownership/PR guards.
scenarioCoverage.reason: Proves the lifecycle transition establishes the correct baseline for strict guards.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Hosted installation-smoke completes successfully without advisory policy changes.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add static ordering regression and run the hosted workflow.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Workflow ordering is changed so archive is after git add or coverage guard.
scenarioCoverage.reason: Prevents recurrence of the bypassed active-to-archive boundary.
